BAIYU Holdings (formerly TD Holdings) is a Shenzhen-based company in commodity trading and supply chain services, especially non-ferrous metals, and precious metals-related financial services, listed on Nasdaq under the symbol BYU. It serves Chinese industrial and trading customers. The input shows about $45 million of funding, last dated November 2021. It is a B2B trading business with little public brand awareness.

Reliance Capital is an Indian financial services company, headquartered in Mumbai and part of Anil Ambani's Reliance Group, with businesses in insurance, asset management, broking and lending, such as Reliance General Insurance and Reliance Nippon Life. It was listed on NSE and BSE but went into insolvency in 2019-2021 and was acquired by IndusInd International Holdings (Hinduja group) through the insolvency resolution process. It was a high-profile consumer finance brand in India.

Decentralized finance company behind the 1inch Network, a suite of crypto products including a DEX aggregator that finds the best prices across exchanges, a liquidity protocol, a wallet, and a limit order and cross-chain swap system. Launched in 2019 by Sergej Kunz and Anton Bukov, it is incorporated in Saint Kitts and Nevis and run through a distributed team, and has its own 1INCH token. Revenue comes from swap fees. Customers are crypto traders. High awareness in the crypto community, and a sponsor in blockchain and sporting events.

Specialist insurance and reinsurance group that buys and manages legacy (run-off) property and casualty books and also runs program management and fronting businesses for insurers. Customers are other insurers and underwriters, and earnings come from run-off profits, fees and acquisition gains. It was listed on London's AIM (ticker RQIH) and operated through Bermuda, London and Guernsey, but ran into solvency and reserving trouble and was delisted around 2023, with subsidiaries going through restructuring. B2B brand with essentially no consumer awareness and weak financial standing for sponsorship.

Swiss healthcare holding company in Fribourg that owns and runs private hospitals and clinics through Swiss Medical Network, along with real estate, hotels and medical technology investments. Customers are patients, insurers and referring doctors, and revenue comes from care fees and property rents. Led by Antoine Hubert, whose family is the main shareholder, and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange. Known in Swiss healthcare and finance.

Indian financial holding company in Chennai that owns Equitas Small Finance Bank, which lends to micro-entrepreneurs, small businesses, vehicle buyers and housing borrowers and takes retail deposits through hundreds of branches. Revenue is mostly from interest on loans. The group began as a microfinance firm in 2007 and is listed on NSE and BSE. Recognised regional consumer finance brand in South India.

Indian non-banking financial company and subsidiary of HDFC Bank, based in Mumbai, lending to small businesses and individuals through loans against property, consumer loans, vehicle finance and gold loans, as well as providing business process outsourcing services. Customers are retail borrowers and small enterprises. It went public in 2025, and operates through hundreds of branches. Backed by a trusted parent brand, with solid recognition across India.

Zillow Group runs the largest US online real estate marketplace, with Zillow, Trulia, StreetEasy, HotPads and Out East brands. Consumers search homes for sale and rent and see Zestimate valuations, while revenue comes from advertising and lead fees from agents, rental listings, and mortgage products via Zillow Home Loans. It exited the iBuying business in 2021. Founded in 2006 and listed on Nasdaq (Z, ZG), Zillow has roughly 200 million monthly users and revenue of about 2 billion dollars. It is a household name in the US with heavy brand advertising and some sports marketing, so a plausible North American sponsor.

CARE Ratings is one of India's major credit rating agencies, based in Mumbai, rating bonds, bank loans, commercial paper and companies' debt for corporates, banks and infrastructure issuers. It also offers advisory and analytical services and operates in India, Africa (via CARE Ratings Africa) and Nepal. Revenue comes from rating fees. It was set up in 1993 and promoted by IDBI Bank, Canara Bank and other institutions, and is listed on BSE and NSE (CARERATING). A B2B institution known mainly to financial professionals and issuers rather than consumers, so it has low public brand visibility.

GHL Systems is a Malaysian payments company providing electronic payment terminals, merchant acquiring, e-payments, and loyalty and transaction processing services for merchants across Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries. Revenue comes from device sales, transaction fees and managed services. It was listed on Bursa Malaysia (GHLSYS) and was taken over by Global Payments of the US, which acquired it in 2022 and delisted it. B2B payments brand known to retailers and banks in Southeast Asia, with little consumer-facing profile.

Ladenburg Thalmann Financial Services was a US diversified financial services holding company, with independent broker-dealer networks (Securities America, Triad Advisors, Investacorp, KMS Financial Services), plus insurance brokerage and asset management. It served financial advisers and their retail clients, earning commissions and advisory fees, and was headquartered in Miami, Florida, with roots in an old New York investment bank. Listed on NYSE American (LTS), it was acquired by Advisor Group in 2020 in a deal worth roughly 1.3 billion dollars. B2B within financial advice, with little brand awareness among consumers.

NSTC is a Beijing-based Chinese financial technology and information services business. Crunchbase tags it as finance and information technology, and shows a sizeable yuan funding round. I cannot confirm exactly what it does or who owns it. It is likely a B2B software or financial information supplier to institutions in China, with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Safeguard Scientifics is a US holding company that provides capital and strategic support to early-stage technology businesses in healthcare technology, fintech and software, taking minority and majority stakes. Its past holdings included Clarient, Alliance Consulting, Sanchez Computer Associates and Prophet 21. It was founded in 1953 and is based in Radnor, Pennsylvania, and listed on the NYSE and later OTC (SFE). It earns returns from selling its stakes. Little consumer awareness, and it is a financial vehicle rather than a brand, so not a typical sponsor.

Computer Age Management Services (CAMS) is India's largest registrar and transfer agent for mutual funds, handling investor records, transactions, KYC and servicing for fund houses that together manage the majority of Indian mutual fund assets. It also offers insurance repository, payment aggregator and digital services via platforms like CAMSPay and CAMSonline. Customers are asset managers and regulators, and revenue comes from per-folio and per-transaction fees. Promoted by HDFC Bank and later partly owned by Great Hill Partners, it listed on BSE and NSE (CAMS) in 2020. B2B, with low consumer awareness.

Jernigan Capital was a US real estate investment trust that provided development and acquisition funding to self-storage owners and developers, taking equity stakes in the properties it financed, and had a handful of self-storage properties of its own. Based in Memphis, Tennessee, it was listed on the NYSE (JCAP). In 2020 it was acquired by NexPoint Real Estate Finance and merged away, and it no longer exists as a separate company. A financial real estate vehicle with no consumer profile.

Srei Infrastructure Finance was an Indian non-banking finance company headquartered in Kolkata that lent to infrastructure and construction-equipment buyers, through Srei Equipment Finance and the parent Srei Infrastructure Finance. Founded in 1985 and listed on the BSE and NSE (SREINFRA), it was among India's leading infrastructure lenders, but defaulted on debts, and in 2021 the Reserve Bank of India superseded its board and began insolvency proceedings. Both entities have been resolved under the insolvency process, with a sale to the National Asset Reconstruction Company in 2023. No longer active as a brand.

Yiren Digital is a Chinese online financial services platform, formerly CreditEase's Yirendai, that connects borrowers with lenders and investors and provides wealth management and consumer credit products, now mostly through institutional funding and its 'Yiren Wealth' arm. Customers are Chinese retail and small-business borrowers and investors, and revenue comes from platform and service fees. Based in Beijing and listed on the NYSE (YRD). It is part of the wider CreditEase group. Known in Chinese fintech circles but not a mainstream consumer brand abroad.

Australis Capital is a Canadian investment company based in Alberta with an interest in the cannabis sector, tagged by Crunchbase as financial services. I cannot confirm specifics of its current holdings or operations. It is a small financial and investment company, thought to be listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange. Little consumer brand awareness, and cannabis ties limit sponsorship use. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Blue Lion is a Hangzhou-based Chinese financial services and fintech business. Crunchbase tags it only as finance and financial services, and it reports a funding total of about 173 million yuan. I cannot confirm its exact products, regulatory status or owner. It likely serves Chinese retail or small business customers online, with no wider brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chesswood Group is a Canadian specialty finance company that, through Pawnee Leasing and Tandem Finance in the US, provides equipment leasing and financing for small businesses, with leases for items like trucks, restaurant gear and medical equipment, sourced via vendors and brokers. Customers are small and mid-size US businesses, and revenue comes from interest and fees on its lease and loan book. Headquartered in Toronto and listed on the TSX (CHW). A B2B lender with no consumer brand awareness.

Global Blockchain is a Hong Kong-based cryptocurrency and blockchain company (Global Blockchain Technologies / Global Blockchain Mining) that held and mined digital assets and invested in blockchain ventures, listed in Canada. Crunchbase lists it as bitcoin and blockchain with funding in Canadian dollars. I cannot confirm details of its operations or ownership. A small, speculative business with limited consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

IP Group is a UK-listed intellectual property commercialisation and venture company that invests in spinouts from universities and technology businesses, including past stakes in Oxford Nanopore, Featurespace and Hinge Health. It earns returns by selling or listing its holdings, and manages a portfolio valued at a few hundred million pounds. Founded in 2001 as IP2IPO and based in London, it is listed on the London Stock Exchange (IPO). A financial holding company that is little known to the public.

Net1 UEPS Technologies (now Lesaka Technologies) is a South African fintech company that runs payment and financial services for unbanked and underbanked consumers and small businesses: social grant payments through its UEPS technology, prepaid airtime, bill payments, lending and insurance, and merchant services via Cash Connect and Kazang. Based in Johannesburg and listed on Nasdaq (LSAK, formerly UEPS) and the JSE. Renamed Lesaka in 2021. Customers are millions of low-income South Africans and thousands of merchants. Some local brand recognition in South Africa through its payment and merchant services, little elsewhere.

PayRight is an Australian fintech in Sydney that offers buy-now-pay-later and instalment financing, with its PayRight product letting consumers pay for purchases, such as medical, veterinary and home services, in fixed instalments. It reports roughly 27 million dollars of funding and sells through merchants and healthcare providers. Private and relatively small, with consumer exposure mainly through partner merchants. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

UK payments business based in Crewe, Cheshire, providing fuel cards, EV charging cards, telematics and fleet services to fleet operators and small businesses, with acceptance at large networks of UK fuel stations. Customers include haulage firms, tradespeople and van fleets, and revenue comes from fuel margins and fees. Moderate brand profile within the UK fleet industry, with little awareness among ordinary motorists.

about: Bharat Financial Inclusion was a Mumbai-based Indian microfinance company, formerly SKS Microfinance, which gave small loans to low-income women in rural India through joint liability groups. It served millions of borrowers across the country, with a large branch network and loans funded by banks, and was listed on the BSE and NSE. SKS had a 2010 IPO and a later crisis during Andhra Pradesh's microfinance ban. It renamed itself in 2015 and merged into IndusInd Bank in 2019. Strong rural brand in India while independent, with little foreign consumer awareness.

Based in the Netherlands and Nevada, it went public on Nasdaq via a SPAC in 2023 under MVLA, later restructuring amid financial pressure. B2B with strong standing in sports technology circles but little general consumer recognition.

Consumer-facing fintech brand with strong awareness among European retail investors.

about: Digital payments and mobile engagement company, formerly BillMyParents, that offered prepaid cards for teens and later mobile marketing tools for businesses. about: ONEOK is a US midstream energy company that gathers, processes, fractionates and transports natural gas, natural gas liquids and refined products via about 60,000 miles of pipelines, serving producers and utilities. Revenue near 33 billion dollars. Headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma; founded 1906. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (OKE). B2B infrastructure operator whose brand is known locally in Oklahoma, naming rights to ONEOK Field in Tulsa.

Indian Oil Corporation is India's flagship state-owned oil company, based in New Delhi, with refining (about 80 million tonnes a year), pipelines, marketing and the largest retail fuel network in India with over 38,000 fuel stations under IndianOil, XtraPremium and Servo lubricants. Revenue is more than 8 trillion rupees. Majority owned by the government of India, listed on NSE and BSE (IOC). Very high consumer awareness in India and a big sponsor in cricket and motorsport.

Caturus is a US oil and gas company providing natural gas and LNG, described in the input as an energy and natural resources firm. Reported funding is about $10.35 billion, indicating a large capital-intensive gas and liquefaction business. No further reliable detail on its owners, assets or customers is available. B2B energy with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Constellation Energy is a Baltimore-based US energy company, listed on Nasdaq (CEG), spun out of Exelon in 2022, and the country's largest producer of carbon-free electricity through its nuclear fleet. It sells power, natural gas and energy services to homes, businesses and utilities, and agreed to acquire Calpine in 2025. Revenue is around $24 billion. Strong brand in energy retail, with limited sponsorship profile.

Energy Transfer is a Dallas, Texas-based US midstream energy company (NYSE: ET), owning one of the largest pipeline networks for crude oil, natural gas, NGLs and refined products across the US, plus Sunoco fuel distribution. It earns fees and distribution margins from producers, refiners and utilities, with assets of about 130,000 miles of pipeline. Led by Kelcy Warren. B2B infrastructure with limited consumer exposure beyond Sunoco-branded fuel.

MPLX is a Findlay, Ohio-based US midstream energy partnership (NYSE: MPLX), formed by Marathon Petroleum, which owns pipelines, terminals and gathering and processing assets to move crude, refined products and natural gas liquids. It earns fees from Marathon Petroleum and third parties. Marathon Petroleum owns the majority of the units. B2B infrastructure with little consumer visibility.

Reliance Industries is a Mumbai-based Indian conglomerate, controlled by Mukesh Ambani, with businesses in oil refining and petrochemicals, retail (Reliance Retail), digital services and telecom (Jio Platforms, with over 480 million subscribers), and media and new energy. Revenue is about $100 billion with a listing on the NSE and BSE (RELIANCE). Customers are hundreds of millions of Indian consumers. Very high brand awareness in India, owner of the Mumbai Indians cricket team and a major sports sponsor.

Saudi Aramco is the state-owned oil and gas company of Saudi Arabia, based in Dhahran, and the world's largest producer of crude oil at around 12 million barrels a day, with refining and chemicals interests. About 82 percent owned by the government and listed on the Saudi exchange (2222). It has a major sponsorship profile, including as global partner of Formula 1 (since 2020) and title sponsor of the Aston Martin F1 team.

Targa Resources is a Houston-based US midstream energy company (NYSE: TRGP), operating natural gas gathering and processing plants, NGL pipelines, fractionators and export terminals, mostly in the Permian Basin and on the Gulf Coast. Customers are oil and gas producers and chemical firms. Revenue is around $16 billion. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

Adura is a UK North Sea oil and gas joint venture combining the UK assets of Equinor and Shell, formed in 2025 and based in Aberdeen. It produces oil and gas with output of roughly 140,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day. Owned 50/50 by Equinor and Shell. B2B energy, with no consumer brand awareness. The input shows reported funding of about $3 billion.

about: AltaGas is a Calgary, Alberta-based North American energy infrastructure company (TSX: ALA), with natural gas utilities (WGL in Washington DC, SEMCO), midstream propane export terminals and storage. It serves about 1.7 million utility customers. Revenue is around C$13 billion. Customers are households and energy firms. B2B and regulated utility, with local brand awareness through WGL.

BB Energy is a London-based independent energy trading company, active in trading, chartering, logistics and storage of oil products, fuel oil, crude and related commodities worldwide, with offices in London, Dubai, Singapore, Geneva and Houston. Customers are refiners, utilities, shipping firms and national oil companies, and it earns from trading margins and logistics services. It is privately held and a large commodities trader by volume. B2B, little public brand awareness.

about: Borr Drilling is an offshore drilling contractor that owns and operates a modern fleet of jack-up rigs, working for oil and gas majors and national oil companies in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Mexico and West Africa. Founded in 2016, it is Bermuda-incorporated with management offices in London and Norway and is listed on the NYSE and Oslo Bors (BORR). Revenue comes from day-rate rig contracts. B2B oilfield services company with almost no consumer brand recognition.

Canadian Natural Resources (CNRL) is one of Canada's largest independent oil and natural gas producers, headquartered in Calgary and listed on the TSX and NYSE (CNQ). It produces over 1.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day from oil sands (Horizon, Albian), conventional heavy oil, offshore (North Sea, Africa) and natural gas, selling mostly to refiners and marketers. Revenue is commodity sales. Founded in 1973. B2B upstream producer with limited consumer brand awareness.

Centalion is a Geneva-based energy trading firm active in crude oil, refined products and natural gas, serving refiners, traders and utilities across Europe, Africa and Asia. The reported funding figure appears to reflect large credit or debt facilities rather than equity. It earns trading margins and logistics fees. Privately held and relatively recent as an independent trader. B2B commodity trader with almost no public consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Cheniere Energy is the largest US producer of liquefied natural gas, headquartered in Houston and listed on the NYSE American (LNG). It operates the Sabine Pass terminal in Louisiana and the Corpus Christi terminal in Texas, exporting LNG to buyers across Europe, Asia and Latin America under long-term contracts. Revenue is tolling and sales to utilities, trading houses and energy majors, around 20 billion dollars annually. Founded 1996. B2B energy infrastructure with little consumer visibility.

CNX Resources is a Pittsburgh-area natural gas producer based in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, with operations in the Appalachian Basin including the Marcellus and Utica shales, and is listed on the NYSE (CNX). It produces around 600 billion cubic feet-equivalent annually, selling gas to utilities, marketers and industrial buyers, and also runs midstream and technology ventures. Revenue is natural gas sales and hedging. Origins trace to a coal and gas business founded in the 19th century. B2B energy producer with limited public awareness.

Commonwealth LNG is a developer of a planned liquefied natural gas export terminal at Cameron Parish, Louisiana, with a capacity of about 8.4 million tonnes per year, backed by Kimmeridge Energy and Mubadala Energy. It has signed long-term offtake agreements with commodity traders and energy buyers. Based in Houston. B2B project developer with almost no public brand awareness.
